title: We Trust Fake Doctor Reviews More than Real Ones
paragraphs: When you need to choose a new doctor or dentist, what do you do?

You probably start by looking at online reviews. One survey even found that 60% of American patients choose their healthcare providers based on positive reviews — and 83% trust online reviews more than personal recommendations.
However, a study in Internet Research found that fake provider reviews have become a serious issue, and may lead patients to make poor choices about their healthcare.
Adding to this problem is that fake reviews are often more convincing than real ones.

Researchers collected 35,000 reviews posted between 2015 and 2017 on a popular online Indian medical directory. The reviews included a wide range of healthcare providers, from family medicine to dentistry.
The researchers were able to verify that 8,300 of the reviews were fake — written by the clinics themselves, which they did by exploiting a security flaw in the directory.

The researchers then took a smaller sample of just 5,000 reviews — both real and fake. They found that the fake reviews tended to be longer and more detailed than the real ones, giving more information about symptoms, diagnoses, treatments and medications.
Shockingly, users saw these highly detailed but fake reviews as more helpful and trustworthy than the real ones.
The researchers said real patients usually aren't comfortable including so much information about their health experiences, creating an information gap that fake reviews can exploit.

"A real patient might simply say a doctor was helpful, while a fake review tells a detailed story about symptoms, diagnosis and treatment," explained researcher Aishwarya Deep Shukla from Canada's Simon Fraser University.
He added that people are drawn to stories, and by having information a real patient might not share, fake reviews can have a real influence on whom people trust with their healthcare.

While the research is based on data from a decade ago, Shukla said fake reviews continue to be a problem — one that's made worse by anyone now being able to use AI to quickly generate detailed text saying whatever they want.
